ops.body:
Owner decision 2026-07-27, taken against measured numbers rather than the original
argument. Supersedes the daemon rationale in doc `3d9c793`.

## The old justification is dead

The plan justified the daemon by `em_load_model` at 133 ms, 79% of warm embedding
engine init. The dense lane is dropped (note `1a3f9c7`), so there is no engine and
no such cost.

## The measured case that replaces it

Real runs on this repo and `~/Code/monorepo`:

```
kg.Load (bbolt open + digest match), warm     23-34 us
  materialize Index back into a *kg.Graph     7.32 / 8.77 ms
eval.LoadCorpus                               36.9 / 88.1 ms
stale.Assess (+DefaultPolicy)                 738.8 ms / 10.43 s   peak RSS 1.86 GB
rank.New (BM25 index + PPR prior)             11.6 / 19.7 ms
rank.Ranker.Retrieve, warm                    4.31 / 6.10 ms
end-to-end in a fresh process                 857 ms / 4.46-7.45 s
```

`kg.Load` being 23 us is real but irrelevant on its own, for two reasons the
measurement surfaced:

1. **Shape mismatch.** `rank.New` takes a flat `*kg.Graph`; `kg.Index` exposes only
   `Node`/`Out`/`In`/`Events`/`Counts` random access. Feeding the ranker means a
   full-bucket JSON decode.
2. **The index persists only the graph.** The corpus and the staleness assessments
   are rebuilt every process, and `stale.ScanTree` walking the monorepo worktree is
   the single largest cost anywhere in the system.

So residency amortizes *derived state* — materialized graph, BM25 index, PPR prior,
assessments — not model weights.

## The alternative that was rejected

Persisting corpus and assessments under the same source digest and relaxing the hook
budget to ~100 ms lands at 85-93 ms measured today, and deletes Phase D entirely. The
owner chose the 10 ms target and the daemon instead.

## The transport, settled by measurement

**A "~13.7 ms Go spawn floor" was asserted here first and is FALSE.** Corrected
2026-07-28 against a dedicated run (Apple M5 Max, go1.26.5, `CGO_ENABLED=0
-trimpath -ldflags="-s -w"`, n=400 per lane, interleaved, load average 32):

```
exec /usr/bin/true                     median 4.236 ms
exec hello-world Go binary             median 4.225 ms
exec Go binary importing wire          median 4.448 ms
exec Go wire client + full round trip  median 6.348 ms   p90 9.578
python: connect + handshake + call     median 0.107 ms   p99 0.278
```

A hello-world Go binary is indistinguishable from `/usr/bin/true`; `GODEBUG=inittrace=1`
shows all package init done by 0.77 ms. The 13.7 ms was one particular binary's own
init, never Go's process start. For reference the real 35.9 MB `cc-notes` binary
spawns at 32.4 ms, which is where that figure came from.

**The conclusion survives, for a different reason.** The 4.2 ms is the kernel's
fork/exec, which *any* client pays, and it is 42% of a 10 ms budget. Against a warm
`Retrieve` of 4.31 ms (cc-notes) / 6.10 ms (monorepo), a spawned Go client lands at
10.66 / 12.45 ms — over budget at the median, and at p90 its transport alone consumes
the whole thing. Spending 42-64% of the budget re-entering the kernel to ask for a
`Retrieve` the daemon exists to make fast defeats the point.

**So the transport is Python speaking daemonkit wire directly**, from the interpreter
capt-hook already has running: 0.11 + 4.31 = 4.42 ms (cc-notes) / 6.21 ms (monorepo).
The protocol turns out to be small and conventional — 4-byte big-endian length, a
32-byte fixed header (`wire/frame.go:20`, `:256-288`), JSON only for the handshake and
the response envelope, no Go-specific serialization anywhere. A ~66-line Python client
was built and proved against daemonkit's real codec. Marginal `import socket` costs
0.851 ms once; dropping `struct` for `int.to_bytes` saves another 0.26 ms.

One hard edge: the server compares `identity.WireBuild` by exact string and decodes
the hello with `DisallowUnknownFields` (`wire/server.go:617`, `:1064-1066`), so a
drifted Python client fails loudly at handshake rather than silently.
